drivingQuestion: Why may one not bless over the spices of gentiles, and what does the baraita mean by fire that 'rested' on Shabbat?
outcomeNote: Rav's oqimta stands via R' Chanina of Sura's reading of the mishna; 'rested' is fixed by Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak as rested from labor of transgression, confirmed by a baraita.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הָכָא בִּמְסִבַּת גּוֹיִם עָסְקִינַן, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁסְּתָם מְסִבַּת גּוֹיִם לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הִיא.
segments.en: «Rav Yehuda said» that «Rav said: Here we are dealing with a party» arranged by «gentiles» and the spices used at that party were prohibited because «the parties of gentiles are generally» devoted «to idolatry.»

segments.he: הָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא אֵין מְבָרְכִין לֹא עַל הַנֵּר וְלֹא עַל הַבְּשָׂמִים שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, מִכְלָל דְּרֵישָׁא לָאו בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה עָסְקִינַן!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But from that which was taught in the latter clause» of the mishna: «One may neither recite a blessing over the candle nor over the spices of idolatry,» infer «by implication that» in «the first clause» of our mishna «we are not dealing with idolatry?» There must be a different reason why the spices of gentiles are prohibited.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא מִסּוּרָא: ״מַה טַּעַם״ קָאָמַר: מַה טַּעַם אֵין מְבָרְכִין עַל הַנֵּר וְלֹא עַל הַבְּשָׂמִים שֶׁל גּוֹיִם — מִפְּנֵי שֶׁסְּתָם מְסִבַּת גּוֹיִם לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
segments.en: «Rabbi Ḥanina of Sura said:» These two halakhot are complementary, and the mishna «states» the halakha employing the style of: «What is the reason.» The mishna should be understood as follows: «What is the reason that one may neither recite a blessing over the candle nor over the spices of gentiles? Because the parties of gentiles are generally» devoted «to idolatry» and one may neither recite a blessing over the candle nor over the spices of idolatry.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אוּר שֶׁשָּׁבַת — מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו, וְשֶׁלֹּא שָׁבַת — אֵין מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו. מַאי ״שָׁבַת״ וּמַאי ״לֹא שָׁבַת״?
segments.en: «The Sages taught» in a baraita: «Over fire that rested, one may recite a blessing» in havdala, «and over» fire «that did not rest, one may not recite a blessing.» The Gemara asks: «What is» meant by «rested, and what is» meant by «did not rest?»ב

segments.he: אִי נֵימָא לֹא שָׁבַת מֵחֲמַת מְלָאכָה אֲפִילּוּ מִמְּלָאכָה דְּהֶתֵּירָא, וְהָתַנְיָא: אוּר שֶׁל חַיָּה וְשֶׁל חוֹלֶה — מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו!
segments.en: «If we say» that did not rest means that «it did not rest from labor, even from labor that is permitted? Wasn’t it taught» in a baraita that «over light» that was kindled on Shabbat «for a woman giving birth or a» dangerously «ill person,» for whom one is permitted to perform prohibited labor on Shabbat, «one may recite a blessing» during havdala at the conclusion of Shabbat?

segments.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַאי ״שָׁבַת״ — שֶׁשָּׁבַת מֵחֲמַת מְלֶאכֶת עֲבֵירָה. תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: עֲשָׁשִׁית שֶׁהָיְתָה דּוֹלֶקֶת וְהוֹלֶכֶת כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ, לְמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת מְבָרְכִין עָלֶיהָ.
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: What is» meant by «rested?» Light «that rested from labor of transgression» on Shabbat. However, if the light burned for the entire Shabbat or was kindled on Shabbat in a permissible manner, one may recite a blessing over it. «That» halakha «was also taught» in a baraita: «A lantern that was continuously burning throughout the entire day» of Shabbat, «one may recite a blessing over it at the conclusion of Shabbat.»
